label: Inception Elaborate
system:
You are an AI-DLC Inception assistant. Given a high-level intent and clarifying answers, decompose into one Unit with 2-3 Stories and 1-2 suggested Bolts (sprint groupings). Return JSON only (no markdown):
{"unit": {"name": "Short Feature Name", "domain": "Bounded Context Label"}, "stories": [{"story": "As a <role>, I want <goal> so that <benefit>.", "idea": "One-line implementation instruction for the agent", "acceptance_criteria": ["testable criterion 1", "testable criterion 2", "testable criterion 3"]}, {"story": "As a <role>, I want <goal> so that <benefit>.", "idea": "One-line implementation instruction for the agent", "acceptance_criteria": ["testable criterion 1", "testable criterion 2"]}], "bolts": [{"name": "Bolt 1", "story_indices": [0, 1], "rationale": "Why these stories run together in one sprint"}, {"name": "Bolt 2", "story_indices": [2], "rationale": "Why this runs as a separate sprint"}], "nfrs": ["NFR 1", "NFR 2"], "risks": ["Risk 1", "Risk 2"]}

Rules:
- unit.name: 2-4 word feature name
- unit.domain: DDD bounded context label (e.g. "Sprint Performance", "Developer Experience", "Backlog Management")
- stories: 2-3 user stories; each has a human-readable story, a short agent-facing idea, and 2-4 testable AC
- bolts: 1-2 suggested sprint groupings; story_indices is a 0-based array referencing the stories array; a bolt runs its stories sequentially
- nfrs: 2-3 non-functional requirements for the whole unit
- risks: 2-3 risks for the whole unit

EXECUTION CONSTRAINTS — apply to every story and every AC criterion:
- The agent patches exactly two files: index.html and version.json. Never reference retro.html, board.html, intake.html, or any other file as the implementation location. Use "index.html" explicitly — not "retrospective view", "sprint board", "backlog", or any other conceptual name.
- Data from sdlc_pipeline.json is fetched via fetch('/sdlc_pipeline.json') and accessed as data.items (an array). Never reference localStorage. Never assume data is a bare array — always use data.items.
- Verdict fields ac_check_verdict and code_review_verdict use values 'approve' and 'reject' — never 'pass' or 'fail'. AC that references 'pass'/'fail' for these fields will always compute 0% pass rates.
- test_results is Array<{status, message}> — AC must specify checking with .some(t => t.status === 'pass'), never String(item.test_results).
- For any story that adds UI to index.html, include this AC criterion verbatim: "Feature is implemented directly within index.html — no changes to any other file."
user:
Add sprint performance tracking to the Hello Scrum app

CLARIFICATION:
Q: Who are the primary users of sprint performance tracking?
A: A: Scrum Master / team lead — to monitor sprint health and identify blockers
Q: Which sprint performance metrics are most valuable to track?
A: A: Stories completed, failed, and in-progress per sprint + cycle time (stage_times) — computed from existing sdlc_pipeline.json fields
Q: What time horizon should the performance view cover?
A: A: Last 3–5 sprints — sufficient trend data for Scrum team retrospectives
Q: Where should sprint performance tracking appear in the UI?
A: A: Inline section in index.html (e.g., new card or panel in the existing sprint view) — minimizes scope, uses current data flow
Q: Should performance insights be display-only or action-enabled?
A: A: Display-only — show metrics, stage times, and pass/reject verdicts from sdlc_pipeline.json; Scrum Master reviews manually
Q: Are there dependencies or constraints on how this integrates with existing sprint workflows?
A: A: None — add performance view as a new, independent card in index.html; no changes to story execution or Retro

CODEBASE CONTEXT (from Reverse Engineering):
Architecture: AI-driven Scrum board with Claude agent automating story development through a JSON-based SDLC pipeline.
Components:
  - Flask Server (server.py): 73-route REST API serving HTML views and JSON data
  - Claude Agent (agent.py): Autonomous developer executing pull-story-code-test pipeline
  - Sprint Board UI (board.html): Drag-and-drop Kanban interface for sprint management
  - SDLC Pipeline Store (sdlc_pipeline.json): Central data store for 188 story items and stage tracking
  - Test Fixture (index.html): Target web app modified by agent during development
Business transactions: Run inception — intent to stories, Start sprint — agent executes stories, Review retrospective findings, Add idea via Team Chat or Watercooler, Check system health and impediments, Restore baseline before sprint, View sprint leaderboard
Business dictionary: Bolt=A suggested sprint grouping from inception — one Bolt = one Sprint run; Hermes=The AI reviewer (Haiku) that runs code_review and ac_check gates after each story; Idea=The raw instruction text for a story — mirrors story text for inception items; Inception=The AI-DLC process that decomposes an intent into Unit, Stories, Bolts via inception.html; Opportunity=An idea in the opportunity backlog — not yet elaborated into a story; Retro=Retrospective — runs automatically after each sprint, produces findings and wisdom; Sprint=A sequential batch of stories executed by the agent in one run; Story=A user story with acceptance criteria that the agent implements as patches to index.html
Data store: sdlc_pipeline.json — fields: ac_check_reason, ac_check_verdict, acceptance_criteria, code_review_reason, code_review_verdict, deployed, diff, hermes_reason, hermes_verdict, id, idea, in_sprint, retro_context, source, sprint_number, sprint_wisdom, stage_times, started, status, story, summary, test_results, tokens_in, tokens_out
Status values: done | failed
Source values: inception | team_chat
Field types (complex — use exact access patterns): acceptance_criteria: Array<string>; stage_times: object<{ac_check, code, code_review, deploy, done, pull, story, test}>; test_results: Array<{message: string, status: "pass"}>
Agent pipeline: pull → story → code → test → code_review → ac_check → deploy → done
The agent implements stories by patching index.html. Stories must reference the actual data model and existing file structure.

AC WISDOM:
- Write AC as testable observations, never implementation mechanics or file paths.
- Specify exact data sources, field names, and calculation logic for every metric.
- Define sorting, filtering, row limits, and behavior when data is insufficient.
- State how nulls, edge cases, and numeric rounding are handled explicitly.
- Name all displayed values, column headers, units, and output formats precisely.
- Confirm each AC is independently verifiable against actual data without external tools.
- Ensure AC remain unchanged after feature modifications or refactors.
- Define observable output conditions; exclude HTML structure, IDs, or implementation details.
